meta.title: DPDP Kit
meta.description: An open-source, self-hosted toolkit for complying with India's DPDP law.

home.heading: DPDP compliance, in one place
home.tagline: Know what the law asks, do the work, and keep the proof.

signIn.title: Sign in to DPDP Kit
signIn.description: Enter your work email and we will send you a sign-in link.
signIn.sentBody: If {email} has access, a sign-in link is on its way. It works once and expires in 5 minutes.
signIn.firstRunHint: The first person to sign in becomes the admin. Everyone else joins by invitation.

errors.INTERNAL: Something went wrong. Please try again.
errors.VALIDATION_FAILED: Some of the information you entered is not valid.
errors.FORBIDDEN: You do not have permission to do this.
errors.CONFLICT: That already exists or is in use somewhere else.
errors.RATE_LIMITED: Too many requests. Please wait a moment and try again.
errors.INVITATION_REQUIRED: You need an invitation to sign in. Ask your admin to invite you.
errors.LAST_ADMIN: There must always be at least one admin.
errors.BUILT_IN: This is built in and cannot be changed.
errors.HAS_CONTROLS: It still has controls. Archive them first.

comingSoon.body: This part of DPDP Kit has not been built yet.

frameworks.title: Frameworks
frameworks.description: Turns the law into a list of small jobs, each with one owner and some proof.

policies.title: Policies
policies.description: The 18 policies a company needs under the DPDP Rules, each with an owner, an approver and the proof to keep.

proof.title: Proof
proof.description: Everything the company has to be able to show, and where each stands.

dataMap.title: Data map
dataMap.description: The list of personal data kept, why, for how long, and who receives it.

connections.title: Connections
connections.description: Collects proof from cloud accounts and the code repository without manual uploads.

noticeAndConsent.title: Notice and consent
noticeAndConsent.description: The public page where people read the notice, give or withdraw consent, and file requests.

requests.title: Requests
requests.description: Handles people asking to see, fix or erase their data, or to complain.

breaches.title: Breaches
breaches.description: Walks the team through a personal data breach against the clock.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Emails and in-app notices that keep the work moving.

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.description: Keys that let your own systems talk to DPDP Kit.

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.description: Passwords and keys DPDP Kit uses to reach your other systems.

aiHelp.title: AI help
aiHelp.description: Optional help with drafting. A person always decides.

myWork.title: My work
myWork.description: Everything waiting on one person, in the order to do it.

activity.title: Activity log
activity.description: Every change, with who made it and when. Nothing here can be edited or removed.
activity.emptyFiltered: No changes of that kind yet.
activity.intact: No changes found. All {count} events match their fingerprints.
activity.broken: An event does not match its fingerprint. It may have been edited or removed.

actions.CONTROL_ASSIGNED: Changed the person on {controlId} ({title}) from {before} to {after}
actions.POLICY_APPROVER_CHANGED: Changed the approver of {policyId} ({title}) from {before} to {after}

profile.title: Company profile
profile.description: Plain questions about your company. Policies and the privacy notice use your answers, so one change here updates every document.
profile.unanswered: {count, plural, one {# not answered} other {# not answered}}
profile.legalNote: These limits come from the DPDP Rules as we read them. Confirm them with counsel before you rely on them. Every change is recorded in the activity log.

confirm.body: This limit comes from the DPDP Rules. Change it only if counsel tells you to. The change is recorded in the activity log.

profile.addDescription: For anything a policy should mention that is not asked here, such as your office address.
profile.removeBody: Policies that use it will show it as missing.

general.title: General
general.description: How your company appears on policies, the privacy notice and auditor reports.

companyName.label: Company name
companyName.hint: Use the legal name. It heads every policy and the notice.

website.label: Website
website.hint: Where your public privacy notice lives.

hostingRegion.label: Hosting region
hostingRegion.hint: Where personal data is stored. Rule 15 cares about this.

languagesOffered.label: Languages offered
languagesOffered.hint: The languages your privacy notice is offered in.

dpoName.label: DPO name
dpoName.hint: The person people contact about their data.

dpoEmail.label: DPO email
dpoEmail.hint: Published so people can reach the DPO.

grievanceEmail.label: Grievance email
grievanceEmail.hint: Where complaints and requests are sent.

breachContact.label: Breach contact
breachContact.hint: Who the team calls first when a breach is found.

breachReportWindow.label: Breach report window
breachReportWindow.hint: Time to send the full breach report to the Board (Rule 7).

logKeepPeriod.label: Log keep-for period
logKeepPeriod.hint: How long records of who used personal data are kept (Rule 6).

erasureWarning.label: Erasure warning
erasureWarning.hint: Warning given before inactive accounts are erased (Rule 8).

inactivityErasureAfter.label: Inactivity erasure after
inactivityErasureAfter.hint: For the kinds of company the Rules name (Third Schedule).

leaverAccessWithin.label: Leavers lose access within
leaverAccessWithin.hint: How fast access is removed when someone leaves.

minTls.label: Minimum TLS version
minTls.hint: The oldest way of securing data in transit that you allow.

keyRotation.label: Key rotation
keyRotation.hint: How often encryption keys are replaced.

accessReview.label: Access review
accessReview.hint: How often someone checks who can open what.

maxDataLoss.label: Most data we can lose
maxDataLoss.hint: Backup target: how much recent work can be lost in a disaster.

timeToRestore.label: Time to restore
timeToRestore.hint: Backup target: how long it takes to be running again.

handlesChildrenData.label: Do you handle data of children or people with disabilities?

sendsDataAbroad.label: Do you send personal data outside India?

isSignificantFiduciary.label: Has the government named you a Significant Data Fiduciary?

profile.legalConfirm: I have checked this with counsel and I want to change it.

people.title: People and roles
people.description: One list of everyone who handles personal data. Access decides what a person can do here. Roles are the named jobs that policies refer to, such as the DPO.

accessLevels.title: Access levels
accessLevels.admin: Everything, including people, connections, keys and secrets.
accessLevels.member: Does the work: policies, data map, proof, requests and breaches.
accessLevels.staff: Is a person on record, for example to hold a role. Has no login.
accessLevels.description: Choose one for each person. Only the first three can sign in.

form.name: Name
form.accessHint: Admin, Member and Auditor get an email invitation to sign in. Staff have no login.

leave.title: Mark {name} as left?
leave.body: Their login stops working straight away, any invitation is cancelled, and the roles they hold become vacant. This cannot be undone here.
leave.doneLogin: Their login has been turned off.
leave.doneChecklist: Remove their access to your other systems within {time}.
leave.doneAssignments: {count, plural, one {1 item that named them now falls back to its role or an admin.} other {# items that named them now fall back to their role or an admin.}}

roleHolders.title: Who holds each role
roleHolders.description: Each role has one holder. Policies and controls use these to say who is responsible. A role with no holder falls back to an admin.
roleHolders.dpoNote: The DPO's name and email also fill in the DPO answers in Company profile.
roleHolders.holds: {count, plural, one {1 item open} other {# items open}}

summary.peopleNote: {count, plural, one {1 has left} other {# have left}}
summary.loginNote: {count, plural, one {1 is staff with no login} other {# are staff with no login}}
summary.rolesNote: {count, plural, =0 {Every role has a holder} one {1 role has no holder} other {# roles have no holder}}

policies.hint: The policies that cover this rule. Open one to write it or to approve it.

add.description: A set of rules your company follows besides the built-in ones, such as a customer’s security review or an internal standard. You add its rules next.

form.name: Name

form.sealHint: A short mark, up to 8 characters.

actions.archiveHint: It disappears from the list. You can only archive it once its controls are archived.

ruleActions.addHint: A rule is one requirement of this framework. Controls go under it.

rules.title: The rules and controls
rules.text: They follow the Digital Personal Data Protection Act and its Rules, written up from the prototype framework this project started with.

policies.title: The policies
policies.text: The 18 policies are templates written in plain English from the same source. On first start each is copied to your company, so editing yours never changes the original.

proof.title: The proof
proof.text: The suggested proof comes from what each policy says to keep. Each item was placed under the control whose wording fits best, by matching words, so some may need moving.

review.text: A lawyer has not yet reviewed any of this. Have counsel check the rules, policies and proof before you rely on them.
